event.title: Gadi Eisenkot Emerges as Frontrunner to Form Israeli Government
event.canonical_title: Gadi Eisenkot Emerges as Frontrunner to Form Israeli Government
event.summary: Gadi Eisenkot has become the leading candidate to form a new government in Israel following a coalition deadlock. His rise comes after a key ultra-Orthodox party declined to recommend any candidate, leading to increased support for Eisenkot from various political factions, including Arab parties. Israeli President Isaac Herzog is expected to announce his decision on the matter soon.

timeline.title: Momentum Builds for Coalition Talks in Israel as Eisenkot Gains Support
timeline.summary: Following inconclusive elections, opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot is gaining momentum in his efforts to form a government in Israel. He has received significant backing, including from Arab parties, as President Isaac Herzog prepares to announce who will be tasked with forming the new government. Eisenkot aims to replace long-serving Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

timeline.title: Gadi Eisenkot Assigned to Form New Israeli Government After Elections
timeline.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has officially tasked former military chief Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new government following the inconclusive results of the October 28 elections. Eisenkot, who leads an anti-Netanyahu alliance, has up to six weeks to negotiate a coalition capable of securing a parliamentary majority. The process is expected to be challenging, with potential alliances being politically sensitive.
key_facts: Gadi Eisenkot has been tasked by President Isaac Herzog to form a new government.
The elections held on October 28 did not result in a clear majority for any party.
Eisenkot has up to six weeks to negotiate a coalition.

timeline.title: Eisenkot Faces Coalition Challenge After Presidential Selection
timeline.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, the former army chief, has been tasked with forming Israel's next government after being chosen by the President over incumbent Benjamin Netanyahu. He has 28 days to assemble a ruling coalition amid a divided opposition. Notably, Arab-led parties have expressed their support for Eisenkot, despite his earlier rejection of a coalition with them, as they share a common goal of ousting Netanyahu.

timeline.title: Eisenkot Criticizes Netanyahu's Campaign Against Palestinian Israelis
timeline.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, a candidate for prime minister, has condemned Benjamin Netanyahu's campaign against Palestinian citizens of Israel as 'racist' and an 'anti-state act.' Eisenkot accused Netanyahu of attempting to marginalize and smear the Arab minority in Israel.
key_facts: Gadi Eisenkot criticized Benjamin Netanyahu's campaign.
The campaign targets Palestinian citizens of Israel.
